lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs have stopped dabbling and started dictating. Saturday's 7-2 demolition of Edmonton was more than a road win over McDavid's Oilers; it was a full-team statement, built on 30 saves from Anthony Stolarz, committed work without the puck and a third period that buried the opposition. William Nylander supplied the signature moment, scoring twice to reach 300 NHL goals, while Auston Matthews, Jack Roslovic, Troy Stecher, Zack MacEwen and Vinni Lettieri joined the scoring parade. Toronto is now 7-4, third in the Eastern Conference, with 16 points and a four-game winning streak. The club has also beaten the Rangers 5-4, Columbus 6-2 and San Jose 3-1 during this run. Next comes Monday's 8:30 p.m. visit to Calgary - a chance to prove this surge travels, and that the Leafs' defensive backbone is becoming real rather than merely convenient.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and Toronto's winter has already supplied its first warning: a 79-83 club cannot afford sentimental roster math. The most encouraging current development is unfolding in Arizona, where eight Blue Jays prospects are getting meaningful Fall League work - Aaron Parker is learning left field while hitting .368 with a .500 on-base percentage, Jake Cook has swiped eight bases, and Jake Bloss owns a 2.70 ERA. Those are auditions, not answers. Andres Giménez remains the lineup's left-handed engine, but the need for another corner bat is plain, particularly with George Springer headed toward free agency. The rotation is more urgent still: José Berríos' Tommy John surgery makes 2027 a question mark, and Bowden Francis remains in recovery. Ernie Clement serving as a World Series correspondent is a charming October footnote. What matters next is whether Toronto buys reliable innings and middle-order force before camp turns prospects into necessities.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors have begun the season by making a persuasive argument: size is useful, but force of will travels better. Friday's 112-102 victory over Washington pushed Toronto to 2-0, with Scottie Barnes driving the night with 28 points and 14 rebounds, while RJ Barrett added 23. Kawhi Leonard, back in the city where his championship legend was forged, supplied 16 points and nine rebounds - less a scoring eruption than a reminder that his fingerprints still appear on winning basketball. Toronto sits second in the Atlantic Division, only 0.5 games behind, and the two-game winning streak has genuine substance: the defense has forced 50 turnovers through two games. Nate Bittle is out with a foot injury, a small concern for a team about to face greater length. Tonight's 7 p.m. visit to Minnesota is the first real litmus test - watch whether Toronto's undersized aggression can survive the Timberwolves' towers.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders are losing ground and now have a league-office grievance to carry with them. At 1-4-1, Washington sits fourth in the NFC East, two games behind, with a one-game losing streak and precious little margin for error. The NFL's decision to fine Fred Warner $65,673 for two fourth-quarter hits on tight end Chig Okonkwo - including one involving helmet contact - gave the 23-17 loss to San Francisco a sharper aftertaste. Warner's punishment does not change the scoreboard, but it confirms Washington absorbed punishment that officials failed to police cleanly. Okonkwo is suddenly the player to watch, both for his availability and his response, while the offense must find more than the 17 points it managed against the 49ers. The Giants tie and Colts loss already exposed how narrow this team's margin is. Philadelphia comes to town Sunday, Nov. 1, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC - a division test Washington cannot afford to waste.

article.title: Nylander Scores Twice as Leafs Beat Oilers
paragraphs: William Nylander scored twice, including his 300th NHL goal, as the Leafs beat the Oilers 7-2 in Edmonton. Anthony Stolarz made 30 saves, while Jack Roslovic added a goal and an assist. Toronto is 7-4 and visits the Flames Monday at 8:30 p.m. ET.

The Raptors take a 2-0 record into tonight's 7 p.m. ET visit to Minnesota, though Bittle is out with a foot injury. Kawhi Leonard's return to Toronto has added another storyline around a young team that faces an early test against the Timberwolves. The Jays turn to Arizona Fall League action, where their prospects are being watched, while Brown addressed his squabbles with Tatum.

The Commanders are 1-4-1 and sit fourth in the NFC East. Their next game is against the Eagles on Sunday, November 1, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Fred Warner was fined twice for hits on Commanders tight end Chig Okonkwo, totaling $65,673.
